notes.content: This articulation agreement outlines the preparatory courses required in the major, based on quarter credit hours. National University courses are listed on the left, with their approved (articulated) transfer equivalents on the right. General education and campus requirements for all bachelor’s degrees are detailed in separate agreements, which can be accessed in ASSIST by selecting “General Education/Breadth” on the left panel. Additionally, NU accepts CSU GE Breadth, IGETC, and Cal-GETC certification to fulfill its GE requirements, except for at least one upper-division GE elective. NU allows a maximum of 12 semester units (18 quarter units) of vocational/technical coursework. Transfer courses noted with "Limits Apply to Non-CSU Transferable Courses" will count toward this limit. For more information on this and all degrees at National University, see Program Finder. Changes to this Agreement Major requirements are subject to change. Newly articulated courses are added on a rolling basis, and the articulation status of some courses may be revised or discontinued. For the most current information, please visit ASSIST every quarter and regularly consult with an academic counselor at NU or your institution.

notes.content: Students interested in the Bachelor of Science in Clinical Laboratory Science at NU must reside in California. A maximum of up to (6 courses; 27 quarter units) of Upper-Division Electives may be awarded toward the Bachelor of Science in Clinical Laboratory Sciences degree (MLT to BSCLS), for students who have: Graduated with an Associate Degree in Medical Lab Technician (MLT) from a CA* Laboratory Field Service (LFS) approved MLT training program AND Passed and submit associated transcripts and certificates for either of the following with an unexpired license MLT American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) examination after 6/01/2003 OR MLT American Association of Bioanalysts (AAB) examination after 1/01/2003. *Individuals who have received an Associate’s Degree outside the state of CA in Medical Lab Technician and passed the ASCP or AAB can submit transcripts and certificates to determine eligibility. The BSCLS program will accept BIO 191A and BIO 193A in lieu of BIO201A and BIO 203A. Students with this interest should review the requirements to obtain a Trainee License from the Laboratory Field Services Branch of the California Department of Health on the website at: https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/OSPHLD/LFS/Pages/CLS-Trainee.aspx

Students interested in the Bachelor of Science in Clinical Laboratory Science at NU must reside in California.


A maximum of up to (6 courses; 27 quarter units) of Upper-Division Electives may be awarded toward the Bachelor of Science in Clinical Laboratory Sciences degree (MLT to BSCLS), for students who have:

  1. Graduated with an Associate Degree in Medical Lab Technician (MLT) from a CA* Laboratory Field Service (LFS) approved MLT training program AND
  2. Passed and submit associated transcripts and certificates for either of the following with an unexpired license
  3. MLT American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) examination after 6/01/2003 OR
  4. MLT American Association of Bioanalysts (AAB) examination after 1/01/2003.


*Individuals who have received an Associate’s Degree outside the state of CA in Medical Lab Technician and passed the ASCP or AAB can submit transcripts and certificates to determine eligibility. The BSCLS program will accept BIO 191A and BIO 193A in lieu of BIO201A and BIO 203A.


Students with this interest should review the requirements to obtain a Trainee License from the Laboratory Field Services Branch of the California Department of Health on the website at: https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/OSPHLD/LFS/Pages/CLS-Trainee.aspx

Students interested in the Bachelor of Science in Clinical Laboratory Science at NU must reside in California.

A maximum of up to (6 courses; 27 quarter units) of Upper-Division Electives may be awarded toward the Bachelor of Science in Clinical Laboratory Sciences degree (MLT to BSCLS), for students who have:
Graduated with an Associate Degree in Medical Lab Technician (MLT) from a CA* Laboratory Field Service (LFS) approved MLT training program AND
Passed and submit associated transcripts and certificates for either of the following with an unexpired license
MLT American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) examination after 6/01/2003 OR
MLT American Association of Bioanalysts (AAB) examination after 1/01/2003.

*Individuals who have received an Associate’s Degree outside the state of CA in Medical Lab Technician and passed the ASCP or AAB can submit transcripts and certificates to determine eligibility. The BSCLS program will accept BIO 191A and BIO 193A in lieu of BIO201A and BIO 203A.

Students with this interest should review the requirements to obtain a Trainee License from the Laboratory Field Services Branch of the California Department of Health on the website at: https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/OSPHLD/LFS/Pages/CLS-Trainee.aspx
